summary: Evaluate conventional finite-harmonic and Ronnmark determinants at the same derived equilibrium wavepoint.

capability: Evaluate conventional finite-harmonic and Ronnmark determinants at the same derived equilibrium wavepoint.
operation: evaluate conventional and Ronnmark kinetic determinants
SI equilibrium controls and dimensionless probe ratios to two kinetic dispersion tensors
discovery.boundary: Both paths require finite nonzero signed kz; zero raises ValueError before graph dependencies or scale computation. Standalone Ronnmark roots/scan retain their separate zero-kz domain.

identity.relation: SI equilibrium controls and dimensionless probe ratios to two kinetic dispersion tensors
identity.direction: SI equilibrium controls and dimensionless probe ratios to two kinetic dispersion tensors
identity.definition: The graph derives omega=omega_frac*wn, kx=kx_frac*kn and f=omega/(2*pi), then preserves the original kernel_omega=2*pi*float(f) conversion before calling evaluate_dielectric_response explicitly with method='harmonic_weideman', harmonics=lmx and method='ronnmark'. Both calls share SI species state; branches are read from the ronnmark diagnostics Result. The public return is a Result.
identity.coordinates: wavevector x-z plane, z parallel to B0; kz is an absolute input
identity.boundary: Both paths require finite nonzero signed kz; zero raises ValueError before graph dependencies or scale computation. Standalone Ronnmark roots/scan retain their separate zero-kz domain.
assumptions: All species controls describe one shared equilibrium snapshot.

inputs.name: ms
inputs.description: Mass of each species, entering the thermal speed and cyclotron frequency
inputs.constraints: Finite positive masses, one value per species.

inputs.name: qs
inputs.description: Charge of each species, setting the sign of the cyclotron frequency and coupling terms
inputs.constraints: Finite nonzero charges, one value per species.

inputs.name: ns_unit
inputs.description: Density of each species relative to the reference density
inputs.constraints: Finite positive density ratios matching the species axis.

inputs.name: Ts_unit
inputs.description: Temperature of each species relative to the reference temperature
inputs.constraints: Finite positive temperature ratios matching the species axis.

inputs.name: B0
inputs.description: Background magnetic-field strength, setting the cyclotron frequency and entering the pole-resonance argument

inputs.name: n00
inputs.description: Reference number density, converting relative to absolute density

inputs.name: T00
inputs.description: Reference temperature, converting relative to absolute temperature
inputs.constraints: Finite positive reference temperature in eV.

inputs.name: omega_frac
inputs.description: Angular frequency as a multiple of the wn derived internally by this graph (the source implementation writes w=wf(p)*wcn); the caller supplies a dimensionless ratio and this graph derives the absolute angular frequency
inputs.constraints: Finite ratio producing nonzero angular frequency.

inputs.name: kz
inputs.description: Wavevector component parallel to the magnetic field, entering the parallel-resonance argument
inputs.constraints: Finite nonzero absolute parallel wavenumber, with its actual sign preserved. Zero is rejected before loading graph dependencies or computing scales.

inputs.name: kx_frac
inputs.description: Perpendicular wavenumber as a multiple of the kn derived internally by this graph (the source implementation writes kx=kxf(p)*kn); the caller supplies a dimensionless ratio and this graph derives the absolute perpendicular wavenumber

inputs.name: lmx
inputs.description: Bessel truncation order forwarded as harmonics to method=harmonic_weideman.
inputs.constraints: Non-bool non-negative Python or NumPy integer, default 5. None, bool, floats, other wrong kinds and negative integers raise ValueError before loading dependencies; forwarded as harmonics to harmonic_weideman only.

preconditions: Species arrays are finite, non-empty and shape-compatible; masses, densities and temperatures are positive, with nonzero charge and magnetic field.
The wavepoint and derived frequency/scales are finite, kz is nonzero, and both numerical path domains are satisfied.
supported: Evaluate conventional finite-harmonic and Ronnmark determinants at the same derived equilibrium wavepoint.
excluded: Mode identification, root finding and accuracy outside the tested finite-harmonic or rational-pole approximation.
Zero kz, inputs that violate either numerical path domain, or inputs requiring a different tensor convention.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for nonfinite or zero kz and for lmx that is None, bool, a non-integer or negative, before loading graph dependencies or computing scales. Errors from derive_species_equilibrium_scales and probe_frequency/probe_wavenumber (nonfinite fractions, nonpositive wn/kn) propagate. A derived f=0, including frequency-conversion underflow to zero, retains ValueError; it does not become a tail or tensor failure. Unsupported numeric conversions may propagate their original errors.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises FloatingPointError for a nonfinite or unrepresentable kernel_omega after the original omega -> f -> float(f) -> 2*pi*f conversion, including true finite-Hz conversion overflow. Derived f=0 is instead ValueError. Numerical failures from evaluate_dielectric_response(method='harmonic_weideman') or evaluate_dielectric_response(method='ronnmark') propagate; no fallback determinant or partial Result.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Both determinant paths are direct evaluations with no iteration, so nonconvergence is not a returned state.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping is returned if either determinant path fails.

python.signature: evaluate_kinetic_dispersion_relation(ms, qs, ns_unit, Ts_unit, B0, n00, T00, omega_frac, kz, kx_frac, lmx=5)

example.description: Evaluate both kinetic dispersion paths at one shared derived wavepoint.
example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_kinetic_dispersion_relation
r=evaluate_kinetic_dispersion_relation(ms=[9.1094e-31],qs=[-1.60217662e-19],ns_unit=[1],Ts_unit=[1],B0=1,n00=6.075e19,T00=1000,omega_frac=1,kz=1326.1942478795652,kx_frac=1); assert 'determinant_sum_n' in r and 'determinant_ronnmark' in r
example.expected: Observed PASS: the composed graph returns both finite-harmonic and Ronnmark determinants together with their 3x3 K/D tensors and derived omega, kx and f.

scope: Independent cross-asset anchor: in the cold limit the zero of determinant_ronnmark in omega/omega_n equals the plasma frequency recomputed by the B5 fluid reference helper from omega_p**2 = sum n q**2/(eps0 m) with the declared constants, an independent mpmath reimplementation that shares no code with this port; measured deviation 1.1e-11 at Ts_unit = 1e-4.

The bracket orientation is asserted explicitly -- the determinant is negative 5 percent below the anchor and positive 5 percent above -- because asserting only that the sign changes would be blind to a negation of the whole determinant.

Secondary statement: the two internal evaluation methods agree to 5.5e-7 and that disagreement is saturated between lmx = 12 and lmx = 16 to within 1e-9, which is what a converged harmonic sum means operationally.

The two-method agreement is explicitly secondary because both determinant_sum_n and determinant_ronnmark are returned by the same call: their ratio is invariant under a common rescaling or negation, so it is equivalent-level evidence for those mutations and only constrains the harmonic truncation.
Test matrix: one species with q = m = n00 = T00 = B0 = 1, kz = 1, kx_frac = 1; Ts_unit = 1e-4 for the cold anchor and Ts_unit = 1.0 for the cross-method and lmx statements.

Failure matrix: one assertion per channel -- the root location against the cross-asset anchor, the determinant orientation across the bracket, harmonic saturation in lmx, the declared graph shapes, and the rejection of a zero kx_frac. Precision budget, written before measurement: 1e-9 on the root, 1e-6 on the cross-method difference, 1e-9 on lmx saturation.
known_limitations: kx_frac = 0 raises FloatingPointError because the harmonic sum divides by the transverse wavenumber. That is a parameter error, not an unreachable cold limit, and it is asserted as such so the next caller does not read the failure as a physics boundary.

The absolute scale of the returned determinants is not anchored: this contract asserts where the zero sits, not the magnitude of the determinant there. The `scale` mutation is therefore covered rather than killed, and the magnitude has no owner -- no contract in this repository declares the scale of these determinants.

The semantics of the returned D_* and K_* arrays were not confirmed from the code, so no relation involving them is asserted; the guessed decomposition determinant = D * K was measured at relative residual 1.0 and is therefore not the right relation.

The `swap` mutation is covered rather than killed: it can only act on the multi-element `branches` and `graph_order` arrays, and this contract asserts their declared shapes, not their element order. That order has no owner -- no contract in this repository declares it.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Bounded to one normalized single-species cold case at kz = 1 and kx_frac = 1, with the mode location anchored against the plasma frequency recomputed by an independent cross-asset helper and the harmonic truncation constrained by the two internal methods. Established by the 1.1e-11 agreement of the cold-limit zero with omega_p and by the 5.5e-7 cross-method agreement that saturates in lmx. Excluded scope: the hot-plasma spectrum, mode identity beyond the Langmuir branch, the magnitude of the determinant, and any statement about the deck constants behind the equilibrium.
